Structuring CLI applications, input handling, and separation of concerns

questions.prompt: Which first step is most useful when applying “Command-Line Application Architecture” in a small Dart program?
options: Build a minimal Dart example for Command-Line Application Architecture, predict its behavior, and verify an edge case before integrating it.
Change multiple unrelated parts until the output appears plausible, then skip a repeatable test.
Copy a dependency version without checking its SDK constraint, maintenance, license, or API documentation.
Assume that a successful native run proves the same APIs and behavior are available on web targets.
questions.answer_key: Build a minimal Dart example for Command-Line Application Architecture, predict its behavior, and verify an edge case before integrating it.
questions.explanation: A minimal example and an explicit boundary check make the behavior easier to verify and maintain.

questions.prompt: If a program involving “Command-Line Application Architecture” behaves unexpectedly, which response is most reliable?
options: Suppress the diagnostic first and investigate only if a user reports a production failure.
Treat untrusted JSON or command-line input as statically validated simply because the program uses Dart.
Add an unrelated package or a broad refactor before reproducing the reported behavior.
Reduce the failure to a small case, inspect the complete diagnostic and inputs, verify the documented SDK/target constraints, and test one change at a time.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the failure to a small case, inspect the complete diagnostic and inputs, verify the documented SDK/target constraints, and test one change at a time.
questions.explanation: Reducing a failure and inspecting full diagnostics avoids speculative changes and exposes SDK/platform assumptions.
